stimuli.content:
Hello, everyone. I'm Mr. Hill. Today I'm going to tell you about the English Camp this summer. The camp will be held for three days, from August 7 to August 9, at Hikari Lake Youth House. About thirty students from five junior high schools will join it.
On the first day, you will make groups and cook dinner together. On the second day, you will climb a mountain with teachers from five countries and talk about nature in English. On the last day, each group will make a short play in English and show it to everyone.
When I was a student, I was afraid of making mistakes, so I didn't speak much in English class. But at a camp like this one, I found that people listened to me even when my English was not perfect. Mistakes are a part of learning. So please don't worry, and try to speak a lot. If you want to join the camp, please give the form to your English teacher by July 10. Thank you.
stimuli.title: 問1(ウ)

stimuli.content:
Hello, everyone. Do you have something at home that you don't use because it is broken? Last spring, the *zipper of my favorite bag broke. I thought, "I have to buy a new one." But my grandmother said, "Why don't you take it to the Repair Café?" I had never heard of that place.

The Repair Café is held at the community center in our city on the second Sunday of every month. People bring broken things there, and volunteers help them repair the things. The volunteers are not *professionals; many of them are *retired people who like making or fixing things. ( ① ) When I visited the café, a man named Mr. Kato showed me how to change the zipper. It took about an hour, and my bag looked like new. I was so happy that I decided to join the café as a volunteer.

Now, please look at [[u:this graph]]. It shows the number of things people brought to the Repair Café in the last three years. In 2021, 120 things were brought. Since then, the number has increased every year, and in 2023, it was twice as large as in 2021. Clothes were the biggest part every year. I was surprised that the number of toys grew so much. In 2021, toys were the smallest part, but in 2023, the number became five times larger, and it was the same as the number of bicycles. Mr. Kato told me that many parents come with their children now. ( ② )

Why do more people come to the café? I asked some visitors. One woman said, "My jacket was a present from my mother, so I want to wear it for a long time." A high school student said, "I want to learn how to repair things by myself." I think people are starting to feel that things have stories, and that throwing them away is a *waste.

Of course, not everything can be repaired at the café. Last month, a boy brought a video game machine, but we couldn't fix it because we didn't have the *parts. He looked very sad. ( ③ ) Now the volunteers are making a list of shops that can repair *electronic things, so that we can tell visitors where to go.

Through this activity, I learned two things. First, repairing takes time, but the time makes us love our things more. Second, when we repair things together, we can talk with people of different ages. Before, I didn't talk with older people very much, but now Mr. Kato is one of my best teachers.

Next time something breaks, please don't throw it away soon. Think about repairing it first. You may find a new story with it. Thank you.

Yui (19:15)：OK. See you tomorrow!

（イ）Kaho and Daiki are junior high school students. They are talking with Mr. Hill, their English teacher, about a video contest.

Mr. Hill：Kaho, Daiki, you want to join this contest, right?
Kaho：Yes. We want to make a video about Hikari River. It's our favorite place in our town.
Daiki：Let's start taking videos of the river this weekend!
Kaho：Wait, Daiki. Look at the poster. In Round 1, we only send a plan. If we don't pass it, we can't send a video.
Daiki：You're right. But we have to decide which part of the river we'll show before we write the plan. There are many good places.
Mr. Hill：That's true. After you write the plan, bring it to me. I'll check your English before you send it.
Kaho：Thank you. If we pass Round 1, we want to take videos of the fireworks festival by the river on July 5.
Daiki：Then we'll *edit the video after the festival and send it before the deadline.
Mr. Hill：Good plan. And if you are chosen for the final, you'll need to practice your speech.

rows: Send a plan for your video (in English, about 100 words).
Teams that pass Round 1 (results: June 20) send a 3-minute video.
Show your video and make a speech at Hikari City Hall.

stimuli.content:
（Riku and Mei are junior high school students in Hikari City. They are talking with Ms. Baker, their English teacher from Australia, after school.）

Ms. Baker：Hi, Riku and Mei. What are you working on?

Riku：Hi, Ms. Baker. We are making a report for the Hikari City Nature Contest. Our topic is *swallows.

Ms. Baker：Swallows? The small birds that fly very fast?

Mei：Yes. They come to Japan from southern countries in spring and make their *nests under the roofs of houses and shops. On the shopping street near our school, you can see many nests every year.

Ms. Baker：Interesting. In my town in Australia, I didn't see birds' nests on shops.

Riku：Look at this graph. It shows [[mark:①:the number of swallows' nests on the shopping street]] from 2015 to 2025. From 2015, the number went down for five years. In 2020, there were only twelve nests.

Mei：But in 2021, the shop owners started a project called "Swallow Guard." Since then, the number has gone up again, and last year it was almost the same as in 2015.

Ms. Baker：That's great. What did the shop owners do?

Riku：They put small boards under the nests. The boards catch the swallows' *droppings, so the street stays clean. Before the project, some owners *removed nests because customers didn't like the dirt.

Ms. Baker：I see. So the boards solved the problem.

Mei：We think so, but we are not sure. We want to know how people on the street feel about swallows now.

Ms. Baker：Then why don't you ask them? [[blank:　　　　　　]]

Riku：That's a good idea. We'll make some questions and visit the street this weekend.

（A week later, Riku and Mei are talking with Ms. Baker again.）

Ms. Baker：How was your *survey?

Mei：We asked 20 shop owners and 50 customers, "Are you happy that swallows come to the street?" Here are [[mark:②:the results]].

Riku：Twelve of the twenty shop owners said "Yes." That's more than half. But five owners said "No."

Mei：On the other hand, forty of the fifty customers said "Yes," and only two said "No." Many customers told us that they enjoy watching the baby birds. One woman said she comes to the street with her son every week to see them.

Ms. Baker：So the swallows bring people to the street. That may be good news for the shops, too.

Riku：Yes! That's our idea. We also asked the owners who said "No" about their reasons. Most of them said, "I like swallows, but I'm too busy to clean the boards."

Mei：So we want to ask the volunteer club at our school to help them. If the club members clean the boards once a week, the owners don't have to do it by themselves.

Ms. Baker：Wonderful. Your report is not only about birds. It's about how people and nature can live together.

Riku：Thank you, Ms. Baker. We'll write that in the last part of our report.

b. The number of nests on the shopping street in 2020 was smaller than in 2015.
c. The shop owners started to put boards under the nests before 2015.

e. Most of the customers said that they were not happy about swallows.
f. Riku and Mei are going to ask the shop owners to clean the boards every day.

distractor_analysis.why_wrong: a・e ともに誤り。客の多く（40人）は Yes と答えた。
